post.text: heapify is O(n)?? sir said heappush is log n so n items should be n log n na

replies.text: Pushing n items one by one is O(n log n). heapify is different: it sifts down from the last parent, and most nodes are near the bottom with short paths, so the total is about 2n swaps, i.e. O(n).

post.text: fib(45) recursive takes forever on my laptop. is my laptop bad

replies.text: Your laptop is fine. Naive recursive fib recomputes the same values again and again (O(2^n)). Add memoization with functools.lru_cache and it becomes O(n).

post.text: binary search returning wrong index sometimes, array is [5,1,9,3]

replies.text: Binary search only works on a sorted array. [5,1,9,3] is not sorted, so the halving logic throws away the wrong half. Sort it first (or use a different method).

post.text: quick sort took ages on an already sorted list of 1 lakh items. why

replies.text: If your pivot is the first element, a sorted list makes every split as uneven as possible, which is quick sort's O(n^2) worst case. Pick a random pivot or the middle element.
